headline: Broader Commodities Slide as Precious Metals and Energy Markets Retreat
paragraphs: Brent crude dropped 1.88 percent on the day and plunged over ten percent for the week, while WTI crude fell 1.29 percent. Oil futures turned lower as the market held out hope for Middle East diplomacy despite Iran stating a war deal remains distant. In the energy sector, European natural gas fell further amid lackluster demand.

Precious metals experienced a sharp correction, with gold sliding below the four thousand dollar mark down 0.53 percent on the day and dropping 2.55 percent for the week. Gold prices slipped ahead of the US midterm elections and amid a broader nearly thirty percent crash from all-time highs. Platinum plummeted 3.22 percent daily and 8.78 percent weekly, while palladium sank 3.53 percent to a thirteen-month low. Commerzbank noted that the recent declines in gold and silver are seen as excessive and overdone.

Copper dropped 3.25 percent to a multi-week low as risk aversion gripped industrial metals. The euro traded at 1.1252 against the US dollar, influencing euro-denominated import costs for Irish businesses.
